case_title: MADAN v. STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH
weapon: Licensed guns, rifles and country-made pistols
aggravating_circumstances: Six deaths caused by brutal firing, one witness murdered during trial, terror of accused persons
mitigating_circumstances: Accused's age, no prison offense record, good behavior in prison, no reason to believe he cannot be reformed
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of murder, sentenced to capital punishment
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction, commuted death penalty of appellant 'S' to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, along with other individuals, fired indiscriminately at multiple individuals, resulting in six deaths. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts and medical evidence, including post-mortem reports, to establish the cause of death. The incident occurred in two locations, with the accused firing at individuals who had fled to take shelter. The trial court convicted the accused of murder, imposing capital punishment. The High Court confirmed the conviction but commuted the death penalty for one accused to life imprisonment.
